transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Maya Rodriguez, Jordan Lee (Redwood) - Nina Patel, Mark Rivers, Olivia Chen (Orbit)

Summary: short demo focusing on long context, high TPS, streaming backpressure, and timeout behavior. Walkthrough of Console + API + Optimize recommendations and Dedicated topology for guaranteed SLOs.

Transcript:
00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, i have Maya and Jordan from our team; can you hear me okay?
00:04 Nina: yeah loud and clear, thanks Alex. we're excited, we've had some weird edge cases with long docs + spikes in traffic.
00:11 Alex: great, quick agenda: i'll do a 10-minute product walkthrough, maya will show a live demo of a long-context + high tps run, then we'll do q&a and discuss POC next steps. if anything's unclear just jump in.
00:27 Maya: hi, uh i'm gonna share my screen, just a heads-up console has live metrics so you might see some refreshes.
00:33 Jordan: quick note, we intentionally left the streaming option on so we can show backpressure behavior.
00:40 Mark: can you define backpressure for us real quick? on our side we saw client timeouts when the response stream slowed.
00:46 Maya: sure, in our context backpressure means the downstream client can't consume tokens as fast as the model produces them, or network stalls - it manifests as buffer growth and sometimes client-side timeouts. we simulate it by limiting read throughput on the client.
00:58 Olivia: and how does the Redwood runtime respond? does it pause generation or keep filling buffers?
01:05 Maya: good question, so the runtime keeps generating until token cache thresholds or our backpressure policy triggers; we have two behaviors - pause generation and resume, or route to a lower-latency variant. default hosted path will do soft throttling and if configured, fallback to a smaller model. on Dedicated you can tune the policy more aggressively.
01:26 Nina: okay, and that means in hosted we might see partial replies and higher 99th perc latency?
01:31 Alex: yes, we surface per-token latency and per-request tail latency in the Console; you can set SLO alerting. for Orbit's SLOs we'll probably recommend Dedicated if you need strict 50ms token tail at scale.
01:44 Maya: starting the long-context demo now - i'm loading a 120k token document (we're simulating a concatenated conversation + doc corpus) and then running 500 req/s bursts with varying prefix lengths.
01:56 (screen noises)
02:03 Maya: okay first run: hosted API, default batching, streaming on. you'll see throughput drop as the KV cache warms and then plateau. transcript note: some transcript words may be off, we had a glitch earlier with 'KV' transcribed as 'kay-vee'.
02:21 Alex: a note on KV cache - long-context support relies on sharded K/V streaming so we don't re-encode long prefixes; that reduces per-token compute but uses more memory on the serving node.
02:34 Mark: memory pressure - what are the memory limits per worker and do you evict?
02:38 Maya: workers have configured cache budgets; we evict LRU segments and can spill to local SSD as a safety net. for Dedicated we can increase cache budget or pin segments to avoid eviction for hot keys.
02:49 Olivia: how do you measure the hit rate? we saw hit rates drop with mixed prefixes.
02:54 Maya: Console exposes per-key hit rate and prefix distribution; Optimize suggests grouping similar prefixes and creating a small prefix cache layer to improve locality.
03:06 Nina: okay, what about high TPS? our traffic pattern is bursty: 2k rps for 30s, then quiet.
03:12 Alex: right, we support autoscale in Dedicated with fast warm-up and burst pools. hosted has throttles and suggest using a token bucket at the client to smooth spikes. for 2k rps you probably want Dedicated with autoscale + burst, we can size the GPU pool based on your request distribution.
03:26 Maya: running the 500 -> 2k pattern now, and enabling artificially slow client reads to provoke streaming backpressure.
03:35 Maya: you can already see a few timeouts on the client side - that's the simulated 3s read timeout. Redwood will surface those as partial responses and mark the request as 'client_timeout' in the audit logs.
03:48 Mark: audit logs - do they include token counts and KV keys? we need them for compliance.
03:53 Alex: yes, audit logs include request metadata, token usage, model variant, and status (complete/partial/timeout). full request payloads are optional for retention; we recommend redaction for PII.
04:05 Nina: security wise we need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS integration and proof of data-in-transit encryption.
04:12 Alex: we have SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML/OIDC, and integrations with AWS KMS and HSM. the security pack I'll share includes diagrams and our encryption whitepaper.
04:22 Olivia: for network setup, will we do VPC peering or PrivateLink? we prefer peering but need to know egress rules.
04:29 Alex: both supported; Dedicated private deployments typically use VPC peering or Transit GW, and we document port requirements and egress. Mark, if you can confirm timings we'll include peering steps in the POC runbook.
04:40 Maya: demo notes: when streaming backpressure occurs our default behavior is to cap the in-flight token buffer per connection, and if client-side is too slow we mark and optionally pause the model until client recovers. that prevents unbounded memory usage.
04:55 Mark: is there any scenario where generation continues and we lose the prefix?
04:59 Maya: not lost - we maintain KV state server-side; but the client may not receive tail tokens if they timeout. on retry we can rehydrate KV cache and resume, but there's a small recompute cost.
05:12 Nina: what's the expected recompute overhead?
05:15 Maya: depends on context length - resuming mid-document can cost about 10-30% extra tokens burned for re-encoding the prefix unless you persist KV snapshots near the resume point. Dedicated supports snapshotting and quicker resume.
05:30 Jordan: also note Optimize will recommend quantization profiles and kernel choices to reduce compute for long sequences; sometimes a 4-bit q8 variant gives 1.8x speedup with acceptable quality loss.
05:44 Olivia: any known model regressions we should watch for with quantization + long context?
05:48 Jordan: yes, hallucination risk can tick up in some seq2seq heads; we pair quantization with eval prompt sets - we'll run your evals during POC.
05:58 Maya: starting the POC benchmark run now - we have three lanes: hosted baseline, dedicated small pool, dedicated burst pool. results will post to the Console and I'll export a spreadsheet after the call.
06:09 (demo runs, metric chatter)
06:30 Maya: okay results summary live: hosted baseline 99th token latency spiked >500ms under 2k rps (with long prefixes), Dedicated small pool kept 99th ~120ms, Dedicated burst pool with pre-warmed KV ~80-100ms and lower tail jitter. streaming backpressure caused ~4% partial-response rate on hosted vs ~1% on Dedicated.
06:50 Nina: those numbers look promising. what's the expected unit cost delta?
06:55 Alex: Dedicated will be more predictable cost; per-token compute cost is similar but reserved capacity and autoscale reduce burst unit costs. i'll send a cost projection later.
07:03 Mark: if we do POC, what telemetry do you need from our side?
07:07 Maya: sample payloads, distribution (prefix lengths), target SLOs, and any network constraints; plus a couple of eval prompt sets to check quality.
07:15 Nina: we'll share that by Friday.
07:18 Alex: cool. final Q&A?
07:22 Olivia: one last - client SDK behavior on backpressure: is there automatic reconnect and resume?
07:27 Maya: SDKs include helpers to resume streams and optionally request KV snapshots for faster resume; language SDKs will expose low-level stream read loops so you can implement backoff and checkpointing.
07:40 Nina: sounds good.
07:43 Alex: recap: we'll send pricing + security pack, Maya runs benchmarks and shares results, Orbit shares data and SLOs; if metrics look good we'll kick off a 4-week POC with Dedicated capacity.
07:56 Nina: thanks all, appreciate the demo.
08:00 Alex: thanks everyone - i'll follow up with an email and links.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcript includes minor ASR errors (KV -> kay-vee, small name misspellings). References to shared artifacts: pricing deck link (shared post-call), security pack (link), benchmark spreadsheet (Console export).
